name: Epithelial Tumor of the Appendix

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Digestive System

criteria.description: Histopathological identification of epithelial neoplastic cells in the appendix
Radiologic evidence of appendiceal mass or mucinous lesion on CT or MRI
Positive immunohistochemical staining for CK20 and CDX2 supporting appendiceal epithelial origin

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of epithelial tumor cells in appendix with supportive imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires surgical specimen evaluation; preoperative diagnosis is challenging.

searchTerms: palpable lump in lower right abdomen
mass felt in right lower belly

pathognomonic.notes: Occurs in mucinous epithelial tumors with peritoneal spread

common.symptomName: Chronic right lower quadrant abdominal pain
searchTerms: long-term pain in lower right belly
persistent pain in right lower abdomen

occasional.symptomName: Urinary frequency or urgency due to mass effect
searchTerms: frequent or urgent urination from mass
urinary symptoms due to pelvic growth

rare.symptomName: Hematuria due to invasion of urinary tract
searchTerms: blood in urine from urinary tract invasion

laboratory: Elevated carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) levels in mucinous tumors
Mild leukocytosis in cases with inflammation
imaging: CT scan showing appendiceal mass or cystic dilation
MRI demonstrating mucinous content and peritoneal implants
genetic: KRAS mutations frequently identified in mucinous epithelial tumors
GNAS mutations in low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasms
other: Histopathology revealing mucinous or non-mucinous epithelial neoplasm
Immunohistochemical profile positive for CK20, CDX2

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of mass or mucinous ascites on imaging

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging right lower quadrant mass
Development of mucinous ascites or pseudomyxoma peritonei
Unexplained weight loss with abdominal distension
references: WHO Classification of Tumors Editorial Board. WHO Classification of Tumors: Digestive System Tumors. 5th ed. IARC; 2019.
Misdraji J. Appendiceal mucinous neoplasms: controversial issues. Arch Pathol Lab Med. 2010;134(5):864-870.
Carr NJ, Cecil TD, Mohamed F, et al. A consensus for classification and pathologic reporting of pseudomyxoma peritonei and associated appendiceal neoplasia. Am J Surg Pathol. 2016;40(1):14-26.
